To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the placentae of women with thrombophilic changes, there is increased expression of complement inhibitory proteins DAF and MCP, which is probably a compensatory mechanism for the increased risk of placental damage.
DAF and MCP expression levels are increased in the placental tissues from women with thrombophilic conditions.

the expression levels of DAF, MCP, and C3b in the placentae of women with inherited thromboembolism are higher than in the control placentae, while in the acquired thrombophilic placentae only DAF expression level is higher.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new mechanism of the complement cascade inhibition in the placenta of thrombophilics.
the expression of complement control proteins in the placental tissues of thrombophilias.
the role of the complement system in the pathogenesis of thrombophilia, and the results indicate that it is a protective mechanism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the observed changes in the complement system in the placental tissue of women with thrombophilic changes are a result of the complex interaction of multiple factors, and not only the result of the changes associated with thrombotic disorders.
the expression of complement inhibitory proteins in the placenta may be an effect of prothrombotic state, and not a protective factor.
the increased expression of complement inhibitors in the placentae of thrombophillic women is an effect of the proinflammatory cytokine environment that accompanies thrombophilia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
complement control proteins are expressed in the placenta and may play a role in the protection of the placenta against complement-mediated injury in thrombophilic pregnancies.
the expression of DAF in placentas is increased in women with thromboembolism, regardless of the etiology of the disease.
in thrombophilic pregnancies, the placenta is able to increase its own protection against complement system activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
increased expression of proteins inhibiting complement activation may be an important mechanism protecting against pregnancy loss in thrombophilic pregnancies.

increased expression of DDF and MCP in the placenta of women with thrombophilic disorders is an adaptive response of the placenta to complement activation, which is associated with the development of these diseases.
increased expression of DAV and MCP in placentas may be a compensatory mechanism for the increased activation of complement.
